questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The boiling point of $0. 001M$ aqueous solutions of $NaCl, {Na}_{2}{SO}_{4}, {K}_{3}{PO}_{4}$ and ${CH}_{3}COOH$ should follows the order.
questions.solution:
Elevation in boiling point, ${ΔT}_{b} = i \times {K}_{b} \times m$.~(${K}_{b}$ is constant for a solvent)

If molality $\left(m\right)$ is same, ${ΔT}_{b} ∝$ van't Hoff factor $( i )$~${CH}_{3}COOH$ only partially dissociates,

$∴ i < 2$

$NaCl, {Na}_{2}{SO}_{4}$

and ${K}_{3}{PO}_{4}$ almost completely dissociate to produce $2, 3 and 4$ ions per formula respectively,

$∴ i \approx 2, 3$, and $4$ respectively

$∴$ The order of $i$~$=$ the order of boiling~points

$= {CH}_{3}COOH < NaCl < {Na}_{2}{SO}_{4} < {K}_{3}{PO}_{4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The values of the Henry's law constant of $Ar, {CO}_{2}, {CH}_{4}$ and ${O}_{2}$ in water at $25 ° C$ are $40. 30, 1. 67, 0. 41$ and $34. 86kbar$, respectively. The order of their solubility in water at the same temperature and pressure is
questions.solution:
By Henry's law,&

${p}_{gas} ∝ {X}_{gas}$ (in liquid solution)

and ${p}_{gas} = {K}_{H} \times {χ}_{gas}$

${K}_{H} =$ Henry's law constant.

$∴$ At a given partial pressure of gas,

${K}_{H} ∝ \dfrac{1}{χgas}$

$∴$ The greater the value of ${K}_{H}$, the less its solubility.

Here, ${K}_{H}$ of $Ar > {O}_{2} > {CO}_{2} > {CH}_{4}$.

$∴$ Solubility of ${CH}_{4} > {CO}_{2} > {O}_{2} > Ar$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The plot of total vapour pressure as a function of mole fraction of the components of an ideal solution formed by mixing liquids $X$ and $Y$& is
questions.solution:
According to Raoult's law,

$p = p^{0}χ$

According to Dalton's law of partial pressure,

${p}_{T} = {p}_{x} + {p}_{y}$

${p}_{T} = p^{0}{xχ}_{x} + p^{0}{yχ}_{y}$

$= p^{0}{xχ}_{x} + {p}_y^{0} \left(1 - {χ}_{x}\right)$

${p}_{T} = p^{0}Y + \left(p^{0}x - p^{0}y\right){χ}_{x}$

Thus, total vapour pressure of solution varies linearly with mole fraction of component $X$.

Case $I$, at ${χ}_{X} = 0$

${p}_{T} = p^{0}Y$

Case $II$, at ${X}_{X} = 1$

${p}_{T} = p^{0}Y + p^{0}X - p^{0}Y$

${p}_{T} = {p}_X^{0}

$
